note: Drawing tasks. The student sketches on paper and sends a photo or describes the sketch. Compare it with `reference` (a description and data) and go through `checklist` one item at a time.

am-kinematics-1d.prompt: A particle starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 1.5 m/s^2 for 6 seconds. It then moves at constant speed for 6 seconds, and finally decelerates uniformly to rest in 3 seconds. Sketch the velocity-time graph and mark the key values.
checklist: Both axes are labelled: time (s) on the horizontal axis and velocity (m/s) on the vertical axis.
The graph starts at the origin and rises in a straight line to 9 m/s at t = 6 s.
It stays level at 9 m/s until t = 12 s.
It falls in a straight line to 0 at t = 15 s.
You can say what the gradient and the area under the graph mean (acceleration and distance).

reference.description: Velocity-time graph. It rises in a straight line from 0 to 9 metres per second at 6 seconds, stays level until 12 seconds, then falls in a straight line to 0 at 15 seconds.

am-projectiles.prompt: A ball is hit from level ground with speed 31 m/s at 60 degrees above the horizontal. Ignore air resistance. Sketch the path of the ball (height against horizontal distance) and mark the greatest height and the range.
checklist: Both axes are labelled: horizontal distance (m) on the horizontal axis and height (m) on the vertical axis.
The path starts at the origin and is a smooth arch, not a straight line.
The highest point is about 36.8 m, exactly halfway along the range.
The ball lands on the ground at about 84.9 m, and the second half is a mirror image of the first.

reference.description: Path of the ball: a symmetrical arch from the origin, reaching a greatest height of about 36.8 metres halfway along, and landing about 84.9 metres from the start.

am-differential-modelling.prompt: The population P of a colony satisfies dP/dt = 0.25P, with P = 700 when t = 0 (t in years). Sketch P against t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 10, marking the starting value and the value at t = 10.
checklist: Both axes are labelled: t (years) on the horizontal axis and P on the vertical axis.
The curve starts at (0, 700), not at the origin.
It always rises, and it gets steeper as t increases (the gradient is proportional to P).
It reaches about 8528 at t = 10 and never touches the t-axis.

reference.description: Exponential growth curve. It starts at 700 when t is 0 and rises ever more steeply to about 8528 at t equal to 10.
